case.summary: Case CASE-019 (Card SC-03019-K957): The real-time risk model flagged transaction 4012227 ($412.46, billing mismatch) with a score of 0.89 [EV-545cb4ec]. The card SC-03019-K957 showed three prior transactions averaging $74.35 [EV-5177e48d] and three online transactions within 48 hours of the flagged transaction [EV-2195055c]. The transaction originated from a new device (Samsung SM-G973F) and an anonymous proxy connection in Argentina [EV-5b21c6fa, EV-ca61c122]. The same device profile appears in a prior confirmed fraud case [EV-abb90528], and the customer SC-03019 has a previous fraud case CC-4328 [EV-7f79d48e]. A pattern-and-keyword retrieval also returned a prior account_takeover case [EV-c4fc536e]. The customer reported they did not make the purchases and still possess the card [EV-08775a39].

The transaction was initiated from a previously unseen device (Samsung SM-G973F) [EV-5b21c6fa] via an anonymous proxy IP located in Argentina [EV-ca61c122], both hallmarks of account takeover. ask.question: What evidence supports this verdict?
ask.answer: The verdict is supported by multiple evidence points: a high risk score (0.89) on transaction 4012227 with billing mismatch (EV-545cb4ec); the flagged transaction amount ($412.46) far exceeds the card's average ($74.35) (EV-5177e48d); three online transactions within 48 hours indicating velocity (EV-2195055c); a new, previously unseen device (Samsung SM-G973F) used for the transaction (EV-5b21c6fa); an anonymous proxy connection from Argentina (EV-ca61c122); a prior confirmed fraud case (CC-4328) linked to the same customer/card (EV-7f79d48e); the same device profile appearing in a confirmed fraud case (EV-abb90528); a prior closed case with the same account_takeover pattern (EV-c4fc536e); and the customer's statement denying the purchases while retaining physical card possession (EV-08775a39).
